product_from_film: Pencil creates website, social-post and mobile-app designs on a shared canvas from prompts, with a parallel-agent control.
explains_well: The surf-club/coffee-shop brief remains consistent across three web pages, social cards and mobile layouts, making the expanding output set easy to connect.
unclear: Many colored agent labels and simultaneous changes are visible, but the film does not show how a user selects, reviews or corrects one agent’s result.
product_type: AI design canvas with parallel agents
scenario: A surf-club website request grows into menu and team pages, then social posts and mobile screens before a download invitation.
product_clear_basis: A readable design prompt at 0–3s is followed by multiple artboards and agent labels at 4s, with page content appearing by 9s.

scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 18–32s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 32–41s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Website brief and parallel control → three pages → social/mobile extension → complete canvas → download.

People making coordinated web and marketing designs are the apparent audience.
Artboards progressively gain content while multiple colored agent labels occupy different areas. This shows concurrent-looking work states, not measured execution speed.
Prompt close-ups establish each task, then wide canvas views show the expanding result set.
A dark editor and black layouts use warm coffee/surf photos, white text and red accents; colored agent labels stand apart.
The first prompt was inspected at full size. Closing text is clear; dense canvas copy and individual agent labels are small.
Voice delivery is unverified.

categories.finding: The brief-to-artboard sequence is understandable without a transcript. Agent responsibilities and review steps are less explicit.
Close prompts and changing selection outlines guide attention, though several active areas compete in the wide views.
About 37s show growing designs after the short prompt setup, then roughly 9s close with text.
The final overview visibly contains the requested web, social and mobile formats; no handoff or export follows.
Multiple active labels and accumulating outputs suggest speed and scale; actual viewer response and processing time are unmeasured.
One surf/coffee identity persists across the different formats, giving the breadth a common subject.
Agent concurrency, generation time, autonomy and usable export behavior are not independently verified. The 4x indicator is a UI label, not measured speedup.
Showing related formats on one canvas makes the parallel-work promise visually concrete.
Show one user correction across the output family.
